name: Sony PlayStation
description: Sony's first home console, a CD-ROM machine built around fast 3D polygon hardware. Launched in Japan in 1994, it brought cheap disc media and a broad third-party library to the mainstream and became the first console to pass 100 million units.

specs.cpu: MIPS R3000A-based CPU @ 33.87 MHz with GTE geometry coprocessor
specs.memory: 2 MB RAM / 1 MB VRAM / 512 KB sound RAM
specs.graphics: Sony custom GPU, up to 640×480, 24-bit colour

curiosities: The PlayStation grew out of a failed partnership to build a CD-ROM add-on for the Super Nintendo.
PlayStation game discs have a black-tinted underside to make them easy to tell apart from audio CDs and copies.
Ridge Racer loads entirely into RAM, so players could swap in a music CD while racing.
Sony sold a black hobbyist version called Net Yaroze that let individuals write PlayStation games on a PC.
The PS one, a smaller redesign of 2000, outsold every other console that year, the new PlayStation 2 included.
story: Sony's console grew out of a failed partnership: Nintendo had asked Sony to build a CD-ROM drive for the Super NES, then publicly dropped it in 1991 for Philips. Ken Kutaragi convinced Sony to go on alone, and the PlayStation launched in Japan in December 1994.

Cheap CDs, easy development tools and a fair licensing deal brought in publishers that had struggled with cartridges. Squaresoft moved Final Fantasy VII to it, and Gran Turismo, Metal Gear Solid, Tekken and Crash Bandicoot followed. Sony marketed it to teenagers and adults, not only to children.
It became the first console to sell more than 100 million units, overtook Nintendo and Sega, and made Sony the leading name in home consoles for the next decade.
